news.title: LIVE: Black Challenge arrive in Ghana after historic Amputee World Cup triumph
news.lede: Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have arrived in Accra following their historic victory at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The team return home as world champions after defeating Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final in San Juan de los Lagos, with captain Richard Arthur Opentil scoring the decisive goal in the 32nd minute. Their arrival at Accra International Airport marks the end of a remarkable campaign that saw Ghana recover from a difficult start to claim the country’s first world title in amputee football. The Ghana Football Association had invited supporters and invited guests to welcome the team at the airport, with fans encouraged to wear Ghana jerseys to celebrate the achievement.

news.title: Vietnam’s U17 team turns heads on World Cup debut
news.lede: Vietnam U17 catches the world’s attention. It took Le Sy Bach just four minutes to make football fans around the world take notice of Vietnam at the FIFA U17 World Cup in Qatar. Meeting a corner, the 1.66-metre-tall forward produced a brilliant first-time backheel that sent the ball into the top corner of Belgium’s net. FIFA featured the strike as a highlight in its November 20 matchday video.

news.title: African youngsters make World Cup statement
news.lede: by AHMED MOOLAH in Cairo, ARMANDO DOMINGOS in Maputo & RUDD KONTE in Bamako Africa Bureau MAPUTO, (CAJ News) – AFRICA’S emerging football talent is making an increasingly powerful impression at the FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, with Mali, Egypt, Uganda and Mozambique already securing places in the Round of 32. The continent has sent 10 national teams to the 48-country competition, which runs from 19 November to 13 December, providing an important platform for Africa’s next generation of football stars to showcase their abilities against the world’s best. Mali, runners-up in the 2015 edition, became the first African representatives to qualify after defeating New Zealand 3-0 and Belgium 2-1 in Group G. Their comeback victory against Belgium, inspired by Djigui Koita and Yaya Niang, demonstrated their resilience and attacking quality.

news.title: FIFA victim of cyberattack, files related to World Cup stake sale unaffected
news.lede: PARIS FIFA said on Thursday that it fell victim to a criminal cyberattack, which led to unauthorised access to personal and business information. A person with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters that no files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. The governing body strongly condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, especially personal data, describing such actions as “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”.

news.title: Chief Imam congratulates Black Challenge on historic World Cup triumph
news.lede: The National Chief Imam of Ghana, His Eminence Sheikh Dr Osmanu Nuhu Sharubutu, has congratulated the Black Challenge on their historic triumph at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico, hailing the team for bringing pride and inspiration to the nation. The Ghanaian side defied the odds to clinch the world title, becoming Africa’s second world champions in amputee football after Angola, following a hard-fought victory over Morocco in the final. In a congratulatory message issued through the Office of the Chief Imam, Sheikh Sharubutu praised the team for their courage, discipline, teamwork and unwavering determination, describing their achievement as a powerful demonstration that disability is not inability. “You have made Ghana proud.
